merger_description:
Invest Blue Finance Pty Ltd (**Invest Blue**) is a company limited by shares and a 100% subsidiary of Ironbark Investment Partners Pty Ltd (**Ironbark**). Ironbark, Invest Blue, and any connected entities of Invest Blue are referred to as **Ironbark Group**.

Invest Blue proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Paris Financial Holdings Pty Ltd (the **Acquisition**). Paris Financial Holdings Pty Ltd is the parent company of four entities:

* Paris Lending Pty Ltd – currently 100% owned
* Paris Financial Services Pty Ltd – currently 100% owned
* Paris Financial Pty Ltd – currently 83% owned
* Paris Financial East Melbourne Pty Ltd – currently 80% owned,

together, **Paris Group**.

As part of the Acquisition, Paris Financial Holdings Pty Ltd will also purchase the remaining ownership stakes in Paris Financial Pty Ltd and Paris Financial East Melbourne Pty Ltd to become the full (100%) owner of all four subsidiaries.

Both Ironbark Group and Paris Group operate in the financial services sector. Ironbark Group provides financial advisory, wealth management, and aged care advisory services to individuals, Australian client households, family offices, high net worth clients, and institutional clients. A division of Ironbark Group also provides funds management and trustee services, and certain specialised advisors engaged within Ironbark Group provide accounting and tax advisory services.

Paris Group is a Melbourne-based financial services firm that primarily provides accounting and tax advisory services to small and medium sized enterprises and individuals. It also provides ancillary financial advisory and wealth management services.

determination_table_content.details:
Invest Blue Finance Pty Ltd (Invest Blue), which is a wholly owned
subsidiary of Ironbark Investment Partners Pty Ltd (Ironbark),
applied for a notification waiver in respect of its proposed
acquisition of 100% of the shares in Paris Financial Holdings Pty Ltd
(together with its subsidiaries, Paris Group), as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Invest Blue, is a company limited by shares and a 100%
subsidiary of Ironbark. Ironbark, Invest Blue, and their connected
entities (together, Ironbark Group) provide financial advisory, wealth
management, and aged care advisory services to individuals,
Australian client households, family offices, high net worth clients,
and institutional clients. A division of Ironbark Group provides funds
management and trustee services, and certain specialised advisors
engaged within Ironbark Group provide accounting and tax advisory
services.
The target, Paris Group, is a Melbourne-based financial services firm
that primarily provides accounting and tax advisory services to small
and medium sized enterprises and individuals. It also provides
ancillary financial advisory and wealth management services.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. there is limited horizontal overlap between the types of
services offered by the parties, with Ironbark Group primarily
supplying financial advice and wealth management services
and Paris Group primarily supplying accounting and tax
advisory services
b. there are alternative providers of the types of professional
services supplied by the parties in Melbourne and nationally.
• In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
